title: Set 159

sentences.ko: 카메라만 켜면 폰이 자꾸 멈추고, 그러다 혼자 재부팅돼. 껐다 켜 보는 것도 이미 해 봤으니까 슬슬 배터리 문제인가 싶어.
sentences.text: My phone keeps freezing every time I open the camera, and then it just restarts on its own. I already tried turning it off and on again, so I'm starting to think it's the battery.

alts.text: Every time I open the camera my phone freezes up and then restarts by itself. Already tried turning it off and on, so I'm kinda thinking it's the battery.
My phone repeatedly freezes whenever I open the camera, and it then restarts by itself. I have already tried turning it off and on again, so I am beginning to suspect that the battery is the problem.

sentences.note: **keeps freezing** 는 자꾸 멈춘다는 뜻으로, keep + ~ing 는 어떤 일이 되풀이될 때 씁니다. **on its own** 은 저절로, 혼자서라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 이사 진짜 도와주고 싶어, 진심이야. 근데 그 토요일엔 동생네 애들 봐 주기로 이미 약속했거든. 그래도 일요일에 아직 손이 필요하면 몇 시간 정도는 들를 수 있을 것 같아.
sentences.text: I'd love to help you move, I really would, but I already promised my brother I'd watch his kids that Saturday. If you still need a hand on Sunday, though, I could probably come by for a few hours.

alts.text: Wish I could, but I told my brother I'd watch his kids that Saturday. Still need help Sunday? I can probably swing by for a few hours.

I would truly love to help you move, I really would, but I have already promised my brother that I would look after his children that Saturday. However, if you still require assistance on Sunday, I could likely come by for a few hours.

sentences.note: **need a hand** 는 일손이 필요하다는 뜻입니다. **come by** 는 잠깐 들르다라는 말이고, casual 의 **swing by** 도 같은 뜻으로 더 가볍게 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 자, 애 학교 행사 때문에 나 금요일 밤 전에는 못 떠나. 근데 밤 비행기 타면 토요일 아침 등산 시간에는 맞춰 도착하는 거 맞지?
sentences.text: Okay, so I can't leave until Friday night because of my kid's thing at school, but if we take the late flight, we'd still get there in time for the hike on Saturday morning, right?

alts.text: Friday night's the earliest I can leave, my kid's got a thing at school. But if we grab the late flight, we'd still make the Saturday morning hike, right?
I am unable to leave until Friday evening because of an event at my child's school. However, if we take the late flight, we should still arrive in time for the hike on Saturday morning, shouldn't we?

sentences.note: **in time for** 는 ~에 늦지 않게 맞춰서라는 뜻입니다. **my kid's thing at school** 처럼 thing 은 행사나 일정을 가볍게 가리킬 때 자주 씁니다.

sentences.ko: 우리 팀에 어떤 남자가 자꾸 내가 한 일을 자기가 한 것처럼 가로채거든. 오늘은 회의에서 내 수치를 꼭 자기가 낸 것처럼 보여 줬어. 근데 제일 속상한 건 내가 아무 말도 못 하고 그냥 앉아만 있었다는 거야.
sentences.text: So this guy on my team keeps taking credit for stuff I did, and today he showed my numbers in the meeting like he came up with them himself. And the worst part is I just sat there and didn't say anything.

alts.text: Ugh, a guy on my team keeps taking credit for my stuff, and today he put my numbers up in the meeting like they were his. Worst part? I just sat there and said nothing.

A colleague on my team has repeatedly taken credit for work that I did, and today he presented my figures in the meeting as though he had produced them himself. What troubles me most is that I simply sat there and did not say anything.

sentences.note: **taking credit for** 는 남이 한 일의 공을 가로챈다는 뜻입니다. **came up with** 는 생각해 내다, 만들어 내다라는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 오늘 밤 딸 재우는 데 두 시간 걸렸어. 잠들었나 싶으면 벌떡 일어나서 물 달라, 노래 하나만 더 불러 달라 하는 거야. 그래서 겨우 잠들었을 때는 저녁 먹을 힘도 없었어.
sentences.text: It took me two hours to get my daughter down tonight. Every time I thought she was out, she'd sit up and ask for water or one more song, so by the time she finally fell asleep, I was too tired to even eat dinner.

alts.text: Took me two hours to get my daughter to sleep tonight. Every time I thought she was out, she'd pop up wanting water or another song, so when she finally crashed I was too wiped to even eat dinner.

It took me two hours to get my daughter to sleep this evening. Each time I believed she was asleep, she would sit up and ask for water or for one more song, so by the time she finally fell asleep, I was too exhausted even to have dinner.

sentences.note: **get my daughter down** 은 아이를 재운다는 뜻입니다. **she was out** 은 완전히 잠들었다는 말이고, casual 의 **wiped** 는 녹초가 됐다는 뜻입니다.

reviewed: 1번 한국어 '배터리 문제인가 싶기 시작해' 는 번역투라 '슬슬 배터리 문제인가 싶어' 로 고침
2번 casual 이 'Honestly' 를 장식으로 붙였고, I'd ... help you move 가 text 와 앞부분이 겹쳐서 더 짧은 구어로 새로 씀
2번 formal 이 text 의 'I really would' 다짐을 빼먹어서 되살림
3번 formal 끝의 'is that correct?' 가 어색한 꼬리말이라 'shouldn't we?' 로 고침
3번 한국어 '맞춰 도착하잖아, 그치?' 가 묻는 말투가 아니라서 '도착하는 거 맞지?' 로 고침
5번 formal 의 'put my daughter to bed' 는 침대에 눕히는 것까지라 text 의 재운다는 뜻에 맞게 'get my daughter to sleep' 으로 고침
